en: Taal Volcano in Batangas features a main crater lake situated on Volcano Island inside Taal Lake.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly through a limestone cave into the South China Sea.
The giant Rafflesia flower found in Philippine rainforests can grow up to three feet across.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects a massive coral atoll and a barrier reef.
Hikers on Mount Pulag in Benguet often see a thick sea of clouds forming below the summit.
Lake Sebu in South Cotabato consists of three distinct lakes connected by short rivers and waterfalls.
The famous white sand of Boracay Island in Aklan is made from crushed coral and foraminifera shells.
Callao Cave in Cagayan features a natural chapel illuminated by sunlight shining through a hole in the ceiling.
The Pasig River in Metro Manila flows westward, connecting Laguna de Bay directly to Manila Bay.
Mayon Volcano in Albay displays a perfectly symmetrical cone shape built by layers of hardened lava and ash.
The Philippine eagle found in Mindanao forests features a distinctive, shaggy crest of brown feathers on its head.
The Amihan, or northeast monsoon, brings cool, dry air to the Philippines from November until early March.
